from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: Surprising Collisions", [
            "Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.",
            "A heavy block hits a smaller block.",
            "The smaller block bounces off a wall.",
            "We count every impact between blocks.",
            "The total count reveals mysterious digits."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        block_a = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#FF5733", fill_opacity=1)
        block_b = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#33FF57", fill_opacity=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.play(FadeIn(block_a), FadeIn(block_b))
        self.place_at_grid(block_a, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(block_b, 'C5')
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.play(block_a.animate.move_to(self.grid['C3']), block_b.animate.move_to(self.grid['C4']))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        # Impact point animation (flash) using valid grid position
        impact = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(self.grid['C3'])
        self.play(Flash(impact, color=WHITE, line_length=0.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(block_a.animate.move_to(self.grid['C2']), block_b.animate.move_to(self.grid['C5']))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")
        v1_label = Text("v1", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(block_a, UP)
        v2_label = Text("v2", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(block_b, UP)
        self.play(Write(v1_label), Write(v2_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Conservation of momentum defines the physics.",
            "Elastic collisions preserve kinetic energy.",
            "We visualize this in phase space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Conservation Laws", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        eq = MathTex(r"m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2 = \text{const}", font_size=36)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(eq))
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight m and v
        eq_m1 = eq[0][0:2]
        eq_v1 = eq[0][3:5]
        eq_m2 = eq[0][6:8]
        eq_v2 = eq[0][9:11]
        
        self.play(
            eq_m1.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            eq_m2.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            eq_v1.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            eq_v2.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Add visual representation
        circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(circle), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(circle.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2))
        self.play(circle.animate.shift(LEFT * 2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Connecting Physics to Geometry", [
            "Mass ratio defines the wedge angle.",
            "Phase space paths form circular arcs.",
            "Arc length relates to pi digits.",
            "Collision paths mirror geometric reflections.",
            "This traces a perfect circle."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        wedge = Sector(radius=2, angle=PI/6, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(wedge, 'C3')
        
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'C3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(wedge), FadeIn(dot))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        arc = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI/2, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(arc, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(arc))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(Indicate(arc))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        intersection = Dot(color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(intersection, 'D3')
        self.play(FadeIn(intersection))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        circle = Circle(radius=1, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Grand Reveal", [
            "Collisions map to digits of pi.", 
            "Physics creates transcendental numbers.", 
            "Geometry reveals the hidden sequence."
        ])
        
        # Objects

        geometry_viz = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.3)

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Indicate(combined, color="#FFFF00"))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Physics of Pi: Block Collisions and Transcendental Digits

sections.title: The Hook: Surprising Collisions
sections.content: Introduce the setup: Two blocks on a frictionless surface. Block A has mass M, Block B has mass 1, and a wall sits to the left. We count the total number of collisions (A hitting B, B hitting the wall, B hitting A).
sections.example: If Block A is 100 times heavier than Block B, they collide exactly 31 times. If M = 10,000, they collide 314 times. If M = 1,000,000, they collide 3,141 times.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Conservation Laws
sections.content: Briefly explain the underlying physics: Conservation of momentum and kinetic energy. In 1D elastic collisions, this system maps to a motion in a 2D phase space. Visualize this as a ball bouncing inside a 'wedge' shape on a coordinate plane.
sections.example: Visualizing the phase space: The angle of the wedge is defined by the mass ratio; as the ratio grows, the wedge narrows, forcing the 'ball' to bounce more times before exiting.

sections.title: Connecting Physics to Geometry
sections.content: Explain that as the mass ratio M approaches infinity, the path length in the phase space approach a circular arc. The number of collisions corresponds to the digits of pi because the arc length relates to the angle calculation of the reflections.
sections.example: An animation showing a light ray bouncing between two mirrors angled at alpha = arctan(1/sqrt(M)). As M increases, the 'zig-zag' path traces the circumference of a circle.

sections.title: The Grand Reveal
sections.content: Synthesize the findings: The collision count is a digital manifestation of pi. This turns a discrete mechanical system into a tool for calculating transcendental numbers.
sections.example: Final slide showing a table: Mass M=10^2n -> Collisions = n digits of pi. It’s not magic; it’s the geometry of phase space!
